quests.hint: 'Considering' opens the sentence as a reason.
quests.explanation: 'Considering how much…' sets up the reason, and 'cut corners' is an idiom for doing something less carefully to save effort.
quests.textToSpeak: Considering how much work has gone into this project, it would be a real shame to cut corners on the final stage.
quests.correctAnswer: Considering how much work has gone into this project, it would be a real shame to cut corners on the final stage.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Considering' /kənˈsɪdərɪŋ/ is stressed on SID. 'Corners' /ˈkɔːnəz/. 'Shame' /ʃeɪm/. 'Project' as a noun is /ˈprɒdʒekt/. 'Gone into' links.

quests.hint: 'The first thing I do is' is a rhythm chunk.
quests.explanation: 'Whenever' describes a routine, and the sentence structure is common in professional self-description.
quests.textToSpeak: Whenever there's a change of plan, the first thing I do is check who else it affects before I say anything.
quests.correctAnswer: Whenever there's a change of plan, the first thing I do is check who else it affects before I say anything.

quests.hint: 'On balance' means 'considering everything'.
quests.explanation: 'Neither of the two' takes a singular verb, and 'in the long run' means eventually.
quests.textToSpeak: Neither of the two options is perfect, but on balance I'd say the cheaper one carries fewer risks in the long run.
quests.correctAnswer: Neither of the two options is perfect, but on balance I'd say the cheaper one carries fewer risks in the long run.

quests.hint: 'Far from being' introduces the opposite of what's expected.
quests.explanation: 'Far from + -ing' strongly rejects an assumption, and 'turned out to be' delivers the surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: Far from being a waste of time, the workshop turned out to be the most useful thing we did all year.
quests.correctAnswer: Far from being a waste of time, the workshop turned out to be the most useful thing we did all year.

quests.hint: 'Having read' gives the reason for the frustration.
quests.explanation: 'Having + past participle' shows an earlier action, and 'whether… or…' sets up two possibilities.
quests.textToSpeak: Having read the contract twice, I still can't tell whether the cancellation clause applies to us or only to the supplier.
quests.correctAnswer: Having read the contract twice, I still can't tell whether the cancellation clause applies to us or only to the supplier.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Clause' /klɔːz/ ends in /z/. 'Cancellation' /ˌkænsəˈleɪʃn/. 'Applies' /əˈplaɪz/. 'Supplier' /səˈplaɪə/. 'Contract' as a noun is stressed on CON.

quests.hint: 'We'll have moved' is a quick chunk.
quests.explanation: 'By this time next year' pairs with 'will have + past participle' to describe what will be complete by then.
quests.textToSpeak: By this time next year, I'm hoping we'll have moved into a bigger place and finally started to feel settled.
quests.correctAnswer: By this time next year, I'm hoping we'll have moved into a bigger place and finally started to feel settled.

quests.hint: Rise at the end, and lean on 'tonight'.
quests.explanation: 'Is there any chance you could…' is a soft request, and 'first thing tomorrow' means early tomorrow morning.
quests.textToSpeak: Is there any chance you could take a look at the draft tonight, so we can send it out first thing tomorrow?
quests.correctAnswer: Is there any chance you could take a look at the draft tonight, so we can send it out first thing tomorrow?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Draft' /drɑːft/ starts with /dr/ and ends in /ft/. 'Tonight' /təˈnaɪt/ is stressed on NIGHT. 'First thing' /fɜːst θɪŋ/ has a tricky /stθ/ junction.

quests.hint: Stress 'do' for a gentle contrast.
quests.explanation: 'I do think' adds emphasis, and 'thought through' means carefully planned.
quests.textToSpeak: I can see why they went with the second proposal, but I do think the first was better thought through.
quests.correctAnswer: I can see why they went with the second proposal, but I do think the first was better thought through.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Proposal' /prəˈpəʊzl/. 'Thought' /θɔːt/ starts with /θ/. 'Went with' links: went-with. 'Do' takes the emphasis.

quests.hint: 'Blow over' means fade away.
quests.explanation: 'Wouldn't count on it' is a cautious way to say don't rely on that, and 'just yet' means not now.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a good chance the whole thing will blow over by next week, but I wouldn't count on it just yet.
quests.correctAnswer: There's a good chance the whole thing will blow over by next week, but I wouldn't count on it just yet.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Count on' links: coun-ton. 'Wouldn't' has a silent 'l'. 'Chance' /tʃɑːns/. 'Whole' /həʊl/.

quests.hint: 'Strength' has a difficult ending.
quests.explanation: 'Lies in the fact that' is a spoken-friendly way to point to the main reason.
quests.textToSpeak: The strength of the argument lies in the fact that it's simple enough for anyone to understand without any specialist knowledge.
quests.correctAnswer: The strength of the argument lies in the fact that it's simple enough for anyone to understand without any specialist knowledge.

quests.hint: 'All the more' intensifies.
quests.explanation: 'Which makes… all the more frustrating' shows that a good start sharpened the disappointment.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody expected the first three months to go so smoothly, which makes the problems we're facing now all the more frustrating.
quests.correctAnswer: Nobody expected the first three months to go so smoothly, which makes the problems we're facing now all the more frustrating.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Smoothly' /ˈsmuːðli/ has a voiced /ð/. 'Frustrating' /frʌˈstreɪtɪŋ/. 'Facing' /ˈfeɪsɪŋ/. 'Three months' has /θriː mʌnθs/.

quests.hint: 'Thoroughly' starts with /θ/.
quests.explanation: 'Thoroughly enjoyed' strengthens the verb, and 'but' introduces a mild criticism.
quests.textToSpeak: She thoroughly enjoyed the workshop, but she felt some of the sessions were rather rushed and could have been longer.
quests.correctAnswer: She thoroughly enjoyed the workshop, but she felt some of the sessions were rather rushed and could have been longer.

quests.hint: 'Given that' means 'because of the fact that'.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' sets out the reason first, and 'absorb' means cope with.
quests.textToSpeak: Given that the deadline's been moved twice already, I don't think it's reasonable to expect the team to absorb any further changes.
quests.correctAnswer: Given that the deadline's been moved twice already, I don't think it's reasonable to expect the team to absorb any further changes.

quests.hint: 'I'll be honest with you' introduces a frank admission.
quests.explanation: 'Talking it through' means discussing fully, and 'changed my mind' shows a shift in opinion.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll be honest with you, I wasn't convinced at first, but talking it through with my family changed my mind.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll be honest with you, I wasn't convinced at first, but talking it through with my family changed my mind.

quests.hint: 'One of the things I' is a long lead-in.
quests.explanation: 'How calmly she deals with' turns a quality into a noun clause, and 'being difficult' describes temporary behaviour.
quests.textToSpeak: One of the things I admire most about her is how calmly she deals with people who are being difficult.
quests.correctAnswer: One of the things I admire most about her is how calmly she deals with people who are being difficult.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Admire' /ədˈmaɪə/. 'Calmly' /ˈkɑːmli/ has a silent 'l' in the first syllable. 'Difficult' /ˈdɪfɪkəlt/. 'Deals with' links.

quests.hint: 'After which' points back to the whole period.
quests.explanation: 'After which' is a compact business connector, and 'whether to' introduces an open choice.
quests.textToSpeak: We'd like to propose a three-month trial period, after which both sides can review the results and decide whether to continue.
quests.correctAnswer: We'd like to propose a three-month trial period, after which both sides can review the results and decide whether to continue.

quests.hint: 'Particularly' has five syllables.
quests.explanation: 'Walk me through' asks for a step-by-step explanation, and 'sign off' means give formal approval.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you walk me through how the approval process works, particularly what happens when someone's on leave and can't sign anything off?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you walk me through how the approval process works, particularly what happens when someone's on leave and can't sign anything off?

quests.hint: 'Flag' means raise attention to.
quests.explanation: 'Hit the date' and 'flag problems' are common workplace idioms, and 'as early as possible' stresses urgency.
quests.textToSpeak: If we're going to hit the launch date, we need everyone to flag potential problems as early as possible instead of waiting for the meeting.
quests.correctAnswer: If we're going to hit the launch date, we need everyone to flag potential problems as early as possible instead of waiting for the meeting.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Potential' /pəˈtenʃl/ is stressed on TEN. 'Launch' /lɔːntʃ/. 'Possible' /ˈpɒsəbl/. 'Instead of' links.

quests.hint: 'What strikes me about' introduces an observation.
quests.explanation: 'However strong… happens to be' concedes the strength of the evidence but shows it doesn't change minds.
quests.textToSpeak: What strikes me about the debate is how rarely anyone changes their mind, however strong the evidence on the other side happens to be.
quests.correctAnswer: What strikes me about the debate is how rarely anyone changes their mind, however strong the evidence on the other side happens to be.

quests.hint: 'On the basis of' is one chunk.
quests.explanation: 'Largely down to' means mostly caused by, and 'a bit unfair' is a mild way to disagree.
quests.textToSpeak: It's a bit unfair to judge the whole approach on the basis of one bad experience, especially when it was largely down to circumstances.
quests.correctAnswer: It's a bit unfair to judge the whole approach on the basis of one bad experience, especially when it was largely down to circumstances.

quests.hint: Let your voice fall at the end, on 'up'.
quests.explanation: 'It took so long for anyone to…' uses 'for + person + to', and 'add up' means make sense.
quests.textToSpeak: Why do you think it took so long for anyone to notice that the numbers in the report didn't add up?
quests.correctAnswer: Why do you think it took so long for anyone to notice that the numbers in the report didn't add up?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Notice' /ˈnəʊtɪs/ is stressed on NO. 'Numbers' /ˈnʌmbəz/. 'Didn't add' has a very light /t/. 'Add up' links: a-dup.

quests.hint: 'And yet' introduces a surprising contrast.
quests.explanation: 'And yet' adds a twist, and 'the one we still talk about' is a natural way to refer back to the trip.
quests.textToSpeak: The whole trip was a disaster from start to finish, and yet, looking back, it's the one we still talk about most.
quests.correctAnswer: The whole trip was a disaster from start to finish, and yet, looking back, it's the one we still talk about most.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Disaster' /dɪˈzɑːstə/ is stressed on ZAS. 'Finish' /ˈfɪnɪʃ/. 'Looking back' links. 'Talk about' links: taw-kə-bout.

quests.hint: 'It dawned on me' means I suddenly realized.
quests.explanation: 'Dawned on me' is a natural storytelling phrase, and 'none of us had checked' uses the past perfect.
quests.textToSpeak: We were halfway up the mountain when it dawned on me that none of us had checked the weather forecast.
quests.correctAnswer: We were halfway up the mountain when it dawned on me that none of us had checked the weather forecast.

quests.hint: 'Spent time + -ing' pattern.
quests.explanation: The past perfect 'had told' sets up why they were unprepared, and 'trying to find' adds the purpose.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody had told us the road would be closed, so we spent nearly two hours driving in circles trying to find a way round.
quests.correctAnswer: Nobody had told us the road would be closed, so we spent nearly two hours driving in circles trying to find a way round.

quests.hint: 'Put you on the spot' means make you decide quickly.
quests.explanation: 'I hate to' softens a big request, and 'any chance of you + -ing' is very polite.
quests.textToSpeak: I hate to put you on the spot, but would there be any chance of you covering my shift on Saturday if you're free?
quests.correctAnswer: I hate to put you on the spot, but would there be any chance of you covering my shift on Saturday if you're free?

quests.hint: 'Let us know' is one chunk.
quests.explanation: 'It would be helpful if you could' is a polite deadline request, and 'whether' introduces the information needed.
quests.textToSpeak: It would be really helpful if you could let us know by the end of the week whether you're planning to attend.
quests.correctAnswer: It would be really helpful if you could let us know by the end of the week whether you're planning to attend.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Attend' /əˈtend/ is stressed on TEND. 'Planning' /ˈplænɪŋ/. 'Whether' /ˈweðə/. 'Helpful' /ˈhelpfl/. 'End of' links.

quests.hint: 'Ever since' means from then until now.
quests.explanation: 'It's been bothering me' uses present perfect continuous for a feeling that hasn't stopped.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't want to make things awkward, so I decided to say nothing at the time, but it's been bothering me ever since.
quests.correctAnswer: I didn't want to make things awkward, so I decided to say nothing at the time, but it's been bothering me ever since.

quests.hint: 'Rough idea' is one chunk.
quests.explanation: 'Give me a rough idea of' asks for an estimate, and 'any extras we haven't discussed' drops 'that' in a relative clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you give me a rough idea of what the final cost might be, including any extras we haven't discussed yet?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you give me a rough idea of what the final cost might be, including any extras we haven't discussed yet?

quests.hint: 'Stay in touch' and 'keep them informed' are parallel.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever happens next' opens with reassurance, and the two verb phrases give clear actions.
quests.textToSpeak: Whatever happens next, I think it's important we stay in touch with the client and keep them informed at every stage of the process.
quests.correctAnswer: Whatever happens next, I think it's important we stay in touch with the client and keep them informed at every stage of the process.

quests.hint: 'Overwhelmingly' has five syllables.
quests.explanation: 'It's tempting… but' concedes a natural reaction, and 'overlook the fact that' redirects attention.
quests.textToSpeak: It's tempting to focus on the negatives, but we shouldn't overlook the fact that most of the feedback we received was overwhelmingly positive.
quests.correctAnswer: It's tempting to focus on the negatives, but we shouldn't overlook the fact that most of the feedback we received was overwhelmingly positive.
